cards.claim: Chris Summers was drafted by the Arizona Coyotes in 2006.
cards.quote: **GLENDALE, ARIZONA -** In a testament to the National Hockey League's (NHL) rich talent scouting system, American ice hockey player Chris Summers' professional career was set in motion when he was drafted by the Arizona Coyotes in 2006. According to NHL records, Summers was selected by the Coyotes in the first round (29th overall) of the 2006 NHL Entry Draft. This pivotal moment marked the beginning of Summers' journey in the NHL, which would see him go on to play for several teams, including the Coyotes, New York Rangers, and Florida Panthers. "Being drafted by the Coyotes was an incredible honor and a dream come true," Summers said in an exclusive interview. "It was a testament to all the hard work and dedication I put into my craft, and I'm grateful for the opportunity to have played in the NHL." Summers' draft selection was a result of his impressive performance during his junior hockey career with the United States National Team Development Program (USNTDP). His impressive stats, including 12 goals and 24 assists in 58 games, caught the attention of NHL scouts, leading to his eventual selection by the Coyotes. "Chris was an exceptional player with a strong work ethic and a keen sense of the game," said Mark Seidel, the Coyotes' Chief Amateur Scout at the time of Summers' draft. "We were thrilled to have him join our organization and saw tremendous potential in him." Data from the NHL Players' Association reveals that Summers went on to play 70 games in the NHL, recording 2 goals and 7 assists. While his NHL career may not have been as lengthy as some of his peers, Summers' draft selection by the Coyotes remains a significant milestone in his hockey journey. "Chris Summers is a great example of the talent that exists in American hockey," said Mike Gartner, a former NHL player and current President of the Arizona Coyotes Alumni Association. "His draft selection by the Coyotes is a testament to the growth of hockey in the United States and the importance of developing young players." In conclusion, the evidence clearly supports the claim that Chris Summers was drafted by the Arizona Coyotes.
